title: Great, Windows Compability Issue.
body:
This laptop has been a great one for me so far(about a week), a Ryzen AI 300 (specifically the AI 750) , 32GB of RAM, 1TB of SSD Storage and a great touchscreen for general use and use with the included Stylus, but there are some caveats as mentioned in the title.

For one, Windows/Graphics Drivers on this laptop cause the 2 and 1 screen flipping function to simply well, not function, this is a software issue mostly on the windows/driver side, and can probably be fixed with enough tinkering.

With that being said, if you're looking for a very efficient laptop this probably isn't for you, it has a 3K 120hz (at least the exact laptop i got, while the specs online quote a 1080p 60) screen with pretty strong components, and doesn't last very long under load, this hasn't been a problem for me as i can end up charging it up when it needs to be, but if that's a key thing you're looking for, i wouldn't recommend this laptop.

Another thing: recently i've actually made
this thing overheat while charging on a sofa and it completely protected itself, I thought it was broken but once turning it back off and on to remove the thermal lock after cooling down, it booted right up with no problems at all.

title: Omnibook X Flip AI PC - meets my needs very well
body: Despite challenges ordering, the Omnibook X Flip AI PC has been excellent.  Setup was easy.  I purchased it for 3 things: 1) Documents, 2) Light gaming, 3) E-reader, 4) AI.  Documents and light gaming are smooth (note: Win11 got rid of Wordpad so you need MS Office or an alternative).  My MMO runs at 1920X1200 and can go higher.  Without a strong GPU, heavy gaming is not possible.  Flip feature is cool and works smoothly.  The e-reader is a journey in itself.  From what I can tell, no Windows laptop vendor comes with a built in solution.  I tried many apps and decided on two: Aquile Reader and Sumatra PDF.  Aquile allows lots of text size/dimension tweaking and Sumatra is a lightweight PDF reader (Adobe works fine too but bulkier).  The point I'm trying to come to is the Omnibook X 16" as an e-reader is perfect with the right app.  A giant/long page is harder to read and an over-cropped page feels like a rip off.  The app puts you in control.  The X keyboard was a little "Off" at first (soft click feel and big keys) - I adapted after a week of heavy use.  For gaming, I still use external keyboard/mouse out of habit.  I have not directly used the AI capabilities but there are apps you can load (Windows comes with co-pilot).  I'm looking at GAIA.  Note: In heavy use the laptop can get warm (not hot) so I recommend a cooling pad/flow.  If taken care of the Omnibook X should provide years of service.  Enjoy.

title: Works, but not without issues
body: I purchased this laptop as a replacement for my 6 year old desktop for photo editing. Performance and screen wise, it is stunning. Shockingly fast for something this thin, and quite nice build quality. The downsides are that the fan is perpetually loud when using Adobe products, and it gets quote hot. I've had quite a few software issues as well - the touch screen randomly stopped working and the performance slowed down substantially in the first few weeks, but somehow a BIOS update fixed this. This isn't really something you'd expect to run into in the first few weeks of owning the product. The speakers are also not great, and the battery doesn't last long doing sustained work - maybe 4-5 hours max just using Adobe Lightroom. Overall, it's not great value to be honest - it does not feel like a premium experience especially given the software issues that would be very hard to troubleshoot for the average user.
